newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares rebound strongly, index back above 900.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares rebound strongly, index back above 900.

text.p: The Athens bourse rebounded convincingly climbing a strong 2.74 percent in moderate volume with the benchmark index gaining 24.43 points to settle at 914.82. Market watchers said it was a healthy technical correction.
Stocks regained composure after Thursday's 3.31 plunge.

"Stocks corrected Thursday's extreme plunge, the market is in a technical correction making up previous losses. On fundamentals alone the index should not be trading here but higher. As for the crisis, nobody lost money and no one wanted to sell frantically but couldn't. There was exaggeration," said analyst Emmanuel Varsos at Investment Analysis.

It was the third normal session since a settlement scandal halted trading for almost four days, despite brokers and analysts predicting that it would take time to repair the negative impact on market sentiment and expecting a further slide.

"We had a good bounce-back. It's the law of nature, what goes down must come up. We also saw a flight to quality, investors opting for liquid, sound blue-chips. If you decide to stay in the market you go to quality issues," said fund manager Dimitris Katsabekis at Agricultural Bank Mutual Funds.
"After the dust settles one can look for value elsewhere in other sectors," he said.
On Monday brokers association president resolved a disagreement over a draft bill on the exchange after meeting with National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou.

The Athens general share index closed up 2.74 percent or 24.43 points higher at 914.82 from Friday's 890.39 close after opening at 892.76. Turnover was 5.44 billion drachmas on volume of 2.32 million shares.
